dc6e4011df.q: What does Dr. Fred Moss argue about psychiatric diagnoses and their validity?
dc6e4011df.a: Dr. Moss argues that psychiatric diagnoses are arbitrary and fluid. He states that if you saw a different clinician, you would receive a totally different diagnosis that would change your world in that direction. When someone comes in with five diagnoses, the only thing he knows is that they have seen five clinicians. A diagnosis only means someone gave you a diagnosis that you agreed to take on—nothing more.

fe8d4be068.q: Why did Dr. Fred Moss describe himself as a recovering psychiatrist?
fe8d4be068.a: Dr. Moss became a recovering psychiatrist because he lived a duplicitous life for about half of his career—approximately until 2006—doing things that were not aligned with what he knew was right. He was living a life misaligned with his values, being asked to diagnose and medicate in ways he believed were causing harm rather than good. Starting in 2006, he made paradigmatic shifts, began taking people off medication and diagnosis, and watched them improve dramatically, leading him to leave conventional practice.

577d5e0f21.q: What does Dr. Fred Moss claim is at the heart of all healing?
577d5e0f21.a: Dr. Moss claims that human connection is at the heart of all healing—all healing of all types, of all conditions, everywhere, everyone. He challenges anyone to find something more valuable than human connection and says he will start doing that instead. This principle is central to his philosophy and his book Welcome to Humanity.

4e8d5a9587.q: What is Dr. Fred Moss's core message about confusion and being human?
4e8d5a9587.a: Dr. Moss argues that confusion is a central feature of the human condition and it is okay to be confused as part of life. The confusion and troubles of being human in a crazy world do not need to be pathologized as if something is wrong with the person experiencing them. We become less confused when we join a group we think is unconfused, but confusion itself is not a disorder—it is simply part of being human.
